files.lesson.md: --- order: 20 unit: logs10 node: [AC9M10M02 n2, AC9M10M02 n3] uses: [AC9M9M02 n1, AC9M9M02 n2] # powers of ten and sizes in scientific notation assumes: [AC9M8N02 n1, AC9M8N02 n2] connection: noise-dose title: Reading log scales summary: "On a log scale, equal steps are equal multipliers. Each 3 dB step halves the safe time, and one ruler of powers of 10 fits a blood cell, a hair and the Sun's distance." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A sound meter creeping from 85 to 88 hardly looks like a change. Is it?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8611 url: http://127.0.0.1:8611/index.html readySelector: "#sl-d" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: noise.yml#explain-pic, caption: "Three decibels up, from 85 to 88: the safe time halves, from 8 hours to 4." } explainClip: query: { code: "@noise.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Every 3 dB halves the time" say: "Every three decibels up halves the safe time." clip: - caption: { text: "85 dB: 8 hours.", say: "At eighty five decibels, eight hours." } - wait: 700 - caption: { text: "88 dB: half as long, 4 hours.", say: "Three more decibels, and it is half as long." } - click: Make d bigger - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "91 dB: half again, 2 hours.", say: "Three more, and it halves again." } - click: Make d bigger - wait: 900 --- A worker's sound meter sits on 85 and then creeps up to 88. Three notches on a dial doesn't sound like much, but a sound meter isn't a ruler. ## Predict: three decibels more ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to the safe time at 88 dB shows who takes off three hours (an addition) and who halves it (a multiplication)." check: type: predict q: "A workplace is allowed to expose a worker to 85 dB for 8 hours a day. Every 3 dB more doubles the risk of hearing damage. How many hours is it safe to stay at 88 dB?" options: - "4 hours" - "5 hours" - "6 hours" - "2 hours" actual: "4 hours. Every 3 dB doubles the risk, so you can stay half as long for the same risk: 8 hours, then 4. It's a multiplication each step, not three hours taken off." ``` The safe time at 85 dB is 8 hours. What is it three decibels louder? ## Run: up the dial ```step stage: run insight: "Equal steps along the decibel axis are equal multipliers on the time, so the graph bends down instead of falling in a straight line." try: { playground: board, starter: "noise.yml#run", height: 560 } check: { type: board, text: "Slide the level from 85 up to 88. Read the hours in the table. Was your prediction right?", when: "d = 88" } ``` Slide up another 3 dB, and another. Look at the table and then at the graph. What does the graph do? ## Investigate: halving, and a ruler for sizes ```step stage: investigate insight: "Each equal step on a log scale is the same multiplier. Several steps multiply that multiplier over and over, and the middle of a log ruler is not the average of its ends. Priya averages the ends." tasks: - check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "How many hours is it safe to stay at 97 dB? Use 8 hours at 85 dB, and halve the time for every 3 dB more." steps: - ["$97 - 85 = 12$ dB more", "how far above 85"] - ["$12 \\div 3 = 4$ steps", "each 3 dB is one step"] - ["$8 \\div 2 \\div 2 \\div 2 \\div 2 = 8 \\div 16$", "halve once for each step, four times"] - ["$8 \\div 16 = 0.5$ hours", "half an hour, or 30 minutes"] answer: "0.5" answerLabel: "Hours" feedback: - ["4", "That's 4 steps, but the question wants the hours: halve 8 four times."] - ["0.8", "Halving 4 times divides by 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16, not by 10."] - ["1", "Halving 4 times is dividing by 16."] criteria: - "I found how many 3 dB steps above 85." - "I halved the time once for every step." - "My answer is under 1 hour." explain: "12 dB is 4 steps: 8 ÷ 16 = 0.5 hours, which is 30 minutes." - check: type: question q: "The ruler shows a red blood cell, a hair and the distance to the Sun. Why are its marks 10 times apart each time instead of 1 metre apart?" options: - "The sizes cover so many powers of 10 that 1 metre apart would squash the cell and the hair together, and the Sun off the page" - "Because 10 is an easier number than 1" - "Because the Sun is exactly 10 times bigger than a hair" - "It's only a style: either ruler shows the same picture" answer: 0 feedback: - null - "It isn't about easy numbers. It's that the sizes differ by many powers of 10." - "The Sun's distance is billions of billions of times a hair." - "Equal metre steps would put the cell and hair on top of each other." explain: "A log ruler gives every power of 10 the same space, so tiny and enormous sizes both fit on one page." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#priya" text: "Priya finds the number halfway between 10 m and 1000 m on a ruler like this. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: log-midpoint-average explain: "Line 3: on a ruler with equal steps of ×10 the halfway mark is one ×10 step from each end, 100 m, not the average, 505 m." ``` ### Halving steps Here's one the other way up. 94 dB is the same as 85 dB plus three steps. ```worked 94 - 85 = 9 :: How far above 85 dB. 9 \div 3 = 3 :: Each 3 dB is one step, so 3 steps. 8 \div 2 \div 2 \div 2 :: Each step halves the safe time, so halve 3 times. 8 \div 8 = 1 :: Halving 3 times is dividing by 2 × 2 × 2 = 8: 1 hour. ``` Now try one on paper: 97 dB. Work out the steps first, then type the hours. ### One ruler for sizes Here's a ruler with a mark for every power of 10. Look at where each thing sits. A red blood cell is about $8 \times 10^{-6}$ m, a hair about $7 \times 10^{-5}$ m, and the Earth to the Sun about $1.5 \times 10^{11}$ m. On a ruler with 1 m between marks, the Sun would be miles off the page. ### Find the mistake Read Priya's working. Is the middle of a ruler of ×10 steps the average of its ends? ## Modify: change the level ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a louder level, a level a long way up the dial, and a level below 85 where the multiplier goes the other way." try: { playground: board, starter: "noise.yml#vary", height: 600 } tasks: - hint: ["Use the table for 97 dB.", "A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes."] check: { type: number, q: "How many minutes is it safe to stay at 97 dB?", answer: 30, explain: "97 dB is 4 steps above 85: 8 ÷ 16 = 0.5 hours, which is 30 minutes." } - hint: ["103 − 85 = 18 dB.", "How many 3 dB steps is that?"] check: { type: number, q: "How many minutes is it safe to stay at 103 dB? Give a decimal.", answer: 7.5, explain: "18 dB is 6 steps: 8 ÷ 64 = 0.125 hours, which is 7.5 minutes." } smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Just the steps: how many 3 dB steps is it from 85 up to 103?", answer: 6, explain: "103 − 85 = 18 dB, and 18 ÷ 3 = 6 steps." } - hint: ["82 is 3 dB below 85.", "Going down a step does the opposite of going up."] check: { type: number, q: "Edge case: how many hours is it safe at 82 dB, one step below 85?", answer: 16, explain: "A step down undoes a halving: it doubles the time, 8 × 2 = 16 hours." } ``` ### Thirty minutes ### Further up ### Below the line ## Practise: steps and ruler ```step stage: practise insight: "Reading a 3 dB step as a halving, finding the middle and the gap on a ruler of powers of 10; the review keeps scientific notation fresh." tasks: - check: type: number q: "How many hours is it safe to stay at 91 dB?" answer: 2 feedback: - ["5", "Each 3 dB halves the time. It doesn't take off an hour."] explain: "91 dB is 2 steps above 85: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 hours." - check: type: answer q: "A ruler has marks at 100 and 10 000, with equal steps of ×10 between them. What number is halfway along?" answer: "1000" form: simplified feedback: - ["5050", "That's the average. On this ruler each equal step multiplies by 10."] explain: "From 100, one step is 1000 and the next step is 10 000. Halfway is 1000." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Count the ×10 steps from 100 up to 10 000. How many steps is that?", answer: 2, explain: "100 to 1000 to 10 000: two steps, so halfway is one step in." } - check: type: number q: "On the sizes ruler a hair is near $10^{-4}$ m and the Earth to the Sun is near $10^{11}$ m. The Sun's distance is about $10^{k}$ times a hair. What's $k$?" answer: 15 explain: "From -4 to 11 is 15 steps along the ruler, each ×10, so 10¹⁵." - check: type: number q: "Review: $0.000008$ m written as $8 \\times 10^{k}$ m. What's $k$?" answer: -6 explain: "The point moves 6 places right to reach 8: k = −6." ``` ### Hours ### The middle ### The gap ### Review Scientific notation, from Year 9. ## Make: back to the concert ```step stage: make insight: "Coming back to the noise limit: a loud concert is five 3 dB steps above 85, so the safe time is halved five times, and the comparison with 8 hours is a ratio of 32." tasks: - hint: ["How many dB above 85 is 100?", "Halve the 8 hours once for each 3 dB step."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A concert is 100 dB. Using 8 hours at 85 dB and halving the time for every 3 dB more, how many minutes is it safe to stand there?" steps: - ["$100 - 85 = 15$ dB more", "how far above 85"] - ["$15 \\div 3 = 5$ steps", "each 3 dB is one step"] - ["$8 \\times 60 = 480$ minutes at 85 dB", "turn the hours into minutes"] - ["$480 \\div 2 \\div 2 \\div 2 \\div 2 \\div 2 = 480 \\div 32 = 15$", "halve once for each of the 5 steps"] answer: "15" answerLabel: "Minutes" feedback: - ["0.25", "That's hours. The question wants minutes: × 60."] - ["48", "Halving 5 times is dividing by 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32, not by 10."] criteria: - "I found the 5 steps from 85 to 100." - "I halved once for every step, not once in all." - "My answer is in minutes." explain: "5 steps: 480 ÷ 32 = 15 minutes." - check: type: number q: "The safe time at 100 dB is how many times shorter than the safe time at 85 dB?" answer: 32 feedback: - ["5", "5 is the number of steps. Each step halves, so 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2."] - ["10", "Five halvings is 2⁵ = 32, not 5 × 2."] explain: "5 steps, each halving: 2⁵ = 32 times shorter. 15 minutes against 8 hours (480 minutes) is 480 ÷ 15 = 32." ``` ### Standing at the concert Back to the concert. Work this out on paper first, then type your answer. ### How many times shorter? 85 dB(A) averaged over 8 hours is the workplace exposure standard, and every 3 dB(A) increase doubles the risk of hearing damage: [Workplace exposure standards for noise, SafeWork SA](https://safework.sa.gov.au/workers/your-health-and-safety-at-work/hazardous-noise/workplace-exposure-standards). Halving the time for each step is the lesson's reading of "doubles the risk" (the same total risk in half the time). Sizes: a red blood cell 6 to 8 micrometres and a hair 20 to 200 (we use 70), from [Micrometre, Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micrometre). The Earth's average distance from the Sun, 150 million km: [NASA](https://science.nasa.gov/earth/facts/). **Also used in** - **Earthquakes.** The last lesson: each step up the magnitude scale multiplies the energy by about 32. - **Computing.** Kilo, mega and giga are each 1000 times the one before, so each is an equal step on a ruler of data sizes. ```teacher summary: Students read a decibel scale as steps that multiply (every 3 dB halves the safe time, so 100 dB allows 15 minutes against 8 hours), then use one ruler of powers of 10 to put a blood cell, a hair and the distance to the Sun side by side, and compare two sizes by counting steps (AC9M10M02, nodes 2 and 3). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can read a level on the decibel scale as a number of 3 dB steps. - I can explain why a log ruler is used for sizes that run from tiny to huge. - I can compare two quantities on a log ruler by counting the steps between them. struggle: "Using the average for the middle of a log ruler, or taking hours off instead of halving. Ask students: is each step on the ruler the same amount added, or the same number multiplied?" before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need How big is a step? (the same multiplier each step) and scientific notation. Two ideas: a step on a log scale is a multiplication (halving per 3 dB), and a log ruler gives every power of 10 the same space, so the middle is a multiplication too. The common mistakes are taking hours off per step and averaging the ends of the ruler (Priya's working). Source: SafeWork SA's standard is 85 dB(A) averaged over 8 hours, and every 3 dB(A) increase doubles the risk of hearing damage. The lesson reads "doubles the risk" as "half the time for the same risk", so 88 dB is 4 hours, 91 dB is 2 hours and 100 dB is 15 minutes. That reading is the lesson's own, so check it against SafeWork's published exposure table before you rely on the minutes. The lesson never explains how decibels are calculated, only the 3 dB step. Sizes: red blood cell 6 to 8 micrometres and hair 20 to 200 micrometres (the lesson uses 8 and 70, Wikipedia, Micrometre); the Earth to the Sun about 150 million km (NASA). running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Those who chose 5 hours took 3 hours off for 3 dB." - "Run: ask students to say what the next row of the table will be before they slide." - "Paper: the 97 dB try-one and the concert in Make are worked on paper first. Books out, and look for the steps counted before any halving." - "Investigate: put the ruler on the board and ask where 10⁻² m would sit before they answer the middle question." - "Modify: before 82 dB, ask whether 82 is above or below 85." stuck: - see: A student says 91 dB is 8 − 3 − 3 = 2 hours, and 100 dB is 8 − 15 = a negative time. ask: At 88 dB is the time 3 hours less, or half as long? fix: "Half as long. Halve once for every 3 dB: 15 dB is 5 halvings." - see: A student says halfway between 10 m and 1000 m is 505 m. ask: How many ×10 steps are there between 10 and 1000? fix: "Two. Halfway is one step from each end: 100 m." - see: A student says halving 5 times is dividing by 10. ask: What is 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2? fix: 32. Five halvings divide by 32. stretch: The safe time at 100 dB is 32 times shorter than at 85 dB. The earthquake step was 32 times the energy. Do those two 32s mean the same thing? support: A strip with the decibel levels 85, 88, 91, 94, 97, 100 and the safe time under each, filled in from the left. leads: > Finishes AC9M10M02. Where it leads: exponential graphs and growth and decay (Year 10 Algebra), and science scales that run over many powers of ten. exit: q: How many hours is it safe to stay at 94 dB, if 85 dB allows 8 hours and every 3 dB halves it? a: 1 hour (3 steps, 8 ÷ 8). explain: > Equal steps on a log scale are equal multipliers. On the decibel scale each 3 dB step halves the safe time: 8 hours, 4, 2, 1, and so on. A log ruler puts every power of 10 the same distance apart, so two things $10^{k}$ times apart are $k$ steps apart, and the middle between 10 and 1000 is 100. sources: - title: "Workplace exposure standards for noise (SafeWork SA): 85 dB(A) averaged over 8 hours; every 3 dB(A) increase doubles the risk of hearing damage" url: https://safework.sa.gov.au/workers/your-health-and-safety-at-work/hazardous-noise/workplace-exposure-standards checked: 2026-10-25 - title: "Micrometre (Wikipedia): hair width 20 to 200 micrometres, red blood cell 6 to 8" url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micrometre checked: 2026-10-25 - title: "Earth facts (NASA): the average distance from the Sun, 150 million km" url: https://science.nasa.gov/earth/facts/ checked: 2026-10-25 ```

files.working.txt:
# Priya's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: priya
Priya's ruler has marks at 10 m and 1000 m. She finds the number halfway between them.
The ruler has equal steps of ×10 between its marks.
Halfway between 10 and 1000 is the average of the two.
(10 + 1000) ÷ 2 = 505.
So the halfway mark is 505 m.
# endregion
